note: Government publishers only. Every source below was opened and read directly during this session; no values were taken from secondary commentary.

sources.title: Form 571 - Allowable Annual Rent Increases 2026-27
Learn about rent increases in San Francisco
sources.verifies: Current 1.6% rate; 60% of Bay Area CPI formula; licence requirement; 12-month rule and anniversary dates; 30/90-day notice; no rounding up; base-rent-only rule; additional-occupant prohibition; worked examples.

sources.title: Learn about San Francisco rental laws
sources.verifies: June 13, 1979 coverage line; rent control vs eviction protection; single-family/condo and other partial exemptions; free Rent Board counselling 415-252-4600.

sources.title: Current Rates, including Rent Increase, Relocation, Sec. Deposit
sources.verifies: Cross-check of 1.6% current rate and prior-year rates; security-deposit interest 4.2%; bankable Rent Board fee amounts.

sources.title: The Rent Board Housing Inventory
sources.verifies: Reporting obligation (all owners, even non-landlords); March 1 annual deadline; licence auto-generated for tenant-occupied units; effective dates July 1 2022 / March 1 2023; no monetary penalty for late filing but notice unenforceable without licence; what must be reported.

sources.title: Sec. 37.15 - Reporting Obligations; Licensing
sources.verifies: Verbatim §37.15: reporting duty, licence granted on substantial compliance, suspension during noncompliance, tenant not obligated to pay increased rent during suspension.

sources.title: Banked rent increases
sources.verifies: Banking mechanics, no expiry, no limit, cannot compound or prorate, notice content must state the banked portion, worked 2022-2025 example. Also contains the 24-month statement logged as irregularity F-03.

sources.title: Annual rent increase for multiple years
sources.verifies: Adding multiple years of increases by summing percentages (not compounding); no petition required; 30/35-day notice; base-rent-only.

sources.title: The Rent Ordinance - Chapter 37 Administrative Code (bookmarked PDF, Ord. 6-2-23)
sources.verifies: Verbatim: §37.2(a) base rent; §37.3(a)(1) annual increase = 60% of CPI, never greater than 7%; §37.3(a)(2) banking; §37.3(a)(8) petition for increases above those permitted; §37.3(a)(11) additional occupants; §37.3(b)(1)-(5) notice content and null-and-void rule; §37.10B.

sources.title: Civil Code §827 - notice of change in terms / rent increase
sources.verifies: 30-day notice for increases of 10% or less; 90-day notice for more than 10% (alone or combined with other increases in the prior 12 months); service personally or by mail per CCP §1013.

sources.title: Civil Code §1947.12 - Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482)
sources.verifies: State cap of 5% + CPI or 10%, whichever is lower; and §1947.12(d)(3) exclusion for housing subject to a local ordinance that restricts annual increases below that amount.

sources.title: Civil Code §1954.53 - Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act
sources.verifies: §1954.53(a) owner may set the initial rate for a new tenancy; §1954.53(d)(2) market increase only after the original occupants no longer permanently reside; §1954.53(d)(3) does NOT apply to partial changes of occupancy where an original occupant remains.

sources.title: Government Code §12955 - FEHA housing discrimination
sources.verifies: Unlawful for an owner to discriminate or harass on the listed protected bases (race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran status, genetic information).

sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
sources.title: Housing Discrimination Under the Fair Housing Act
sources.verifies: Federal prohibition on housing discrimination based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, disability. No federal rent ceiling is stated on this page (see F-10).

sources.title: Penal Code §396 - price gouging during a declared emergency
sources.verifies: During a declared state or local emergency (and 30 days after), it is unlawful to charge more than 10% above the prior price for, among other things, housing.

sources.title: The Rent Board Fee
sources.verifies: $59.00 per dwelling unit for the 2026-2027 tax year; due March 1; up to 50% ($29.50) recoverable from a tenant in occupancy on November 1; fee exemption does not satisfy Housing Inventory reporting; late penalties to 15%.

sources.title: Report an unlawful rent increase or request a review of your rent history (Form 516C)
sources.verifies: Tenant remedy: Form 516C petition for unlawful rent increase; no filing fee; no time limit; ALJ arbitration hearing; decision mailed to parties.

sources.title: Tenant Summary Petitions (Form 518)
sources.verifies: Fast-track petition where a rent-increase notice is clearly unlawful on its face; staff contact the landlord; a re-notice sets a new anniversary date.

sources.title: Sec. 37.10B - Tenant Harassment
sources.verifies: Bad-faith conduct definitions, including §37.10B(a)(5) (influencing a tenant to vacate by coercion, with 'rent increase substantially in excess of market rates' listed as evidence of bad faith) and §37.10B(a)(9) (violating discrimination laws); remedies include treble damages, statutory damages, attorney fees, misdemeanour.

sources.title: Algorithmic devices that set rent are prohibited in San Francisco (Sec. 37.10C)
sources.verifies: Section 37.10C took effect October 14, 2024; selling or using revenue-management software that recommends rents or occupancy from non-public competitor data is unlawful; civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; tenants and tenant organisations may sue.

sources.title: Petition for a Determination Pursuant to Section 6.14 and/or Costa-Hawkins
sources.verifies: §6.14 unlimited increase on remaining occupants requires a written 6.14 notice served within a reasonable time (generally 60 days) of learning of the occupancy; §6.14 applies to co-tenants, Costa-Hawkins only to subtenants/assignees who moved in after 1/1/1996.

sources.title: Landlord Petitions and Passthroughs
sources.verifies: Six categories of increase that require a landlord petition filed before the notice (capital improvement, O&M, comparable rents, Prop I history, utility passthrough, §1.21); no filing fee; tenants need not pay until approved.

sources.title: Charging for Additional Occupants Prohibited
sources.verifies: No extra rent solely because a roommate or family member joined the tenancy, even if the lease allows it; remedy is a tenant petition; landlord may instead petition for an O&M increase.

sources.publisher: SF Open Data (City and County of San Francisco)
sources.title: Rent Board Housing Inventory - dataset gdc7-dmcn
sources.verifies: Owner-reported base rents in $250 bands, unit size, occupancy type, year built, by analysis neighbourhood. Query URLs used are listed in data/market.json so each count can be re-run.

sources.title: Index of Landlord and Tenant Information
sources.verifies: Catalogue of every Rent Board topic ID used to locate the primary pages cited here.

sources.title: AB 325 (2025), Chapter 338 - Cartwright Act: common pricing algorithms
sources.verifies: Adds Business and Professions Code §§16729 and 16756.1: unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm in a manner that restrains trade. Chaptered October 6, 2025.

sources.title: Form 1007 - Notice to Tenant required by §37.9(c) (includes Tenant Right to Counsel information)
sources.verifies: Official Rent Board notice stating that tenants are eligible for free assistance through the Tenant Right to Counsel program (Eviction Defense Collaborative, 415-659-9184).

sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD USER)
sources.title: FY 2026 Fair Market Rent Documentation System - San Francisco HUD Metro FMR Area
sources.verifies: Methodology page loaded, but the dollar table rendered empty in this environment. No HUD FMR figure is published on this site (F-08).

sources.title: Rent Board forms (Forms Center)
sources.verifies: Form numbers used in this project: 516C (unlawful rent increase), 518 (tenant summary petition), 537 (§6.14 / Costa-Hawkins landlord petition), 571 (rates), 577 (all rates).

sources.title: Speak with a Rent Board Counselor
sources.verifies: Free weekday counselling for owners and tenants; the channel the Rent Board itself directs owners to when a unit is hard to classify.

sources.title: Overview of covered and exempt units
sources.verifies: The eight categories of residential units entirely exempt from the Rent Ordinance.

sources.title: Property Information Map (build year / unit count lookup)
sources.verifies: The tool the Rent Board tells owners to use to confirm when a building was built and how many units it has — the two facts that decide coverage.
